skill.name: operating-k8s-local
skill.description: Guides local Kubernetes development with Minikube, kubectl workflows, manifests, service access, and common debugging commands.
skill.summary: Run and debug local Kubernetes clusters with Minikube and kubectl.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and expected Kubernetes command examples. Two findings remain confirmed because the local ingress workflow uses sudo to modify /etc/hosts, and a semantic review found placeholder Kubernetes secrets that could be copied into real manifests.

remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning before the sudo tee command and provide a manual edit alternative so users understand the host file change.

remediation.issue: Weak placeholder secrets in Kubernetes examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace password=secret and mysecretpassword with guidance to generate unique local-only values and avoid committing real secrets.

content.value_statement: Local Kubernetes setup can be slow when cluster, image, and networking steps are unclear. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Minikube and kubectl workflows for development and debugging.
actual_capabilities: Start and manage Minikube clusters with memory, CPU, and driver options.
Enable common Minikube addons such as ingress and metrics-server.
Build Docker images directly into the Minikube environment.
Apply Kubernetes manifests for deployments, services, secrets, and ingress.
Debug pods with kubectl describe, logs, exec, port-forward, and top commands.
Access local services through NodePort, LoadBalancer tunnel, port forwarding, or ingress.
limitations: Focuses on Minikube rather than kind, k3d, or cloud-managed clusters.
Does not include Helm chart authoring or advanced production deployment patterns.
Assumes kubectl, Docker, and Minikube are already installed.
Some examples require local admin approval, such as editing the hosts file.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a local K8s workspace
use_cases.description: Set up a Minikube cluster with useful addons and a repeatable local development flow.

use_cases.title: Debug a failing local deployment
use_cases.description: Use kubectl commands to inspect pods, events, logs, resource usage, and service connectivity.

use_cases.title: Test Kubernetes manifests before sharing
use_cases.description: Run deployment, service, config, secret, and ingress examples locally before team review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a local cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the operating-k8s-local skill to help me start a Minikube cluster with enough resources for a small web app.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a local image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the operating-k8s-local skill to show how I can build my Docker image into Minikube and deploy it with imagePullPolicy set for local use.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a broken pod
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the operating-k8s-local skill to diagnose a pod that is CrashLoopBackOff in my Minikube cluster.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a full local workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the operating-k8s-local skill to design a local Kubernetes workflow for API and web services, including image builds, manifests, ingress, and debugging checks.

output_examples.input: Help me access a service running in Minikube.
output: The skill explains NodePort access with Minikube service URLs.
It also describes port forwarding and LoadBalancer access with a Minikube tunnel.
For ingress, it shows the local host mapping step that may require admin approval.

output_examples.input: My pod is not starting in local Kubernetes.
output: The skill directs you to describe the pod and read recent events.
It suggests checking previous container logs for crashes.
It includes resource and network checks for common local failures.

output_examples.input: I need a simple deployment and service manifest.
output_examples.output: The skill provides basic Deployment and Service examples with local image settings, probes, selectors, and ports.

best_practices: Confirm the active kubectl context before applying manifests.
Use local-only image tags and imagePullPolicy settings when testing Minikube builds.
Review any command that changes host networking or system files before running it.
anti_patterns: Do not run sudo commands from examples without understanding the system change.
Do not copy placeholder secret values into shared or production manifests.
Do not apply local manifests to a cloud cluster by mistake.

faq.question: Does this skill install Kubernetes tools?
faq.answer: No. It assumes Minikube, kubectl, and Docker are available on the local machine.

faq.question: Can it help with cloud Kubernetes clusters?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. The examples are focused on local Minikube development, not managed cloud clusters.

faq.question: Does it include debugging commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers pod descriptions, logs, exec, port forwarding, resource usage, and service checks.

faq.question: Why does it mention editing /etc/hosts?
faq.answer: That step maps a local ingress hostname to the Minikube IP. It should be reviewed because it uses admin privileges.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it safe for production Kubernetes?
faq.answer: No. It is a local development guide and does not cover production security, scaling, or cloud operations.
